chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"The shroud should be a burd cloth; if it is not a burd cloth, then make all of it cotton. If you do not find a cotton turban, then make the turban Sābirī cloth."

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: When the one responsible for the deceased wishes to perform his ghusl, he should place him upon a bier or something similar, directed toward the qiblah, with the soles of his feet toward it and his face facing it, according to how he was directed at the time of his death. Then he removes his shirt, if he is wearing one, from above down to his navel, opening or tearing its collar so that it may be widened for removing it. Then he places over his private parts something that covers them. Then he gently softens the fingers of his hands; if they are stiff, he leaves them. He takes sidr and places it in a basin or something similar from clean vessels, pours water over it, then beats it until its foam gathers on the surface of the water; when it has gathered, he takes it with both hands and puts it into a clean vessel such as a basin or washbowl or the like. Then he takes a clean rag and wraps his hand with it from his wrist to the tips of the fingers of his left hand, places upon it some of the ushnan that he had prepared, and washes with it the outlet of feces from him. Another person should be with him pouring water over it, and he washes it until he cleanses it. Then he discards the rag from his hand and washes both of his hands with plain water. Then he performs wudu (ablution) for the deceased: he washes his face and his forearms and wipes his head and the tops of his feet. Then he takes the foam of the sidr and puts it upon his head and washes it, and washes his beard with approximately nine ratls of sidr-water. Then he turns him onto his left side so that his right side appears to him, and washes it from his neck down to beneath his feet with the like of that amount of sidr-water. He does not place him between his legs during washing; rather, he stands at his side. Then he turns him onto his right side so that his left side appears to him, and washes it likewise. Then he returns him onto his back and washes him from the crown of his head to beneath his feet with sidr-water, just as he washed his head, using around nine ratls of sidr-water or more than that. His assistant pours water over him while he wipes whatever part of his body his hand passes over and cleanses him. While washing him he says: O Allah, Your pardon, Your pardon. Then the sidr-water is poured out from the vessels, and plain water is poured into them, and in it he places that small amount of camphor that he had prepared, and washes his head with it as he had washed it with sidr-water, and washes his right side, then the left, then his chest, as we mentioned in the first washing. Then whatever remains in the vessels of the camphor-water is poured out, and plain water in which there is nothing is placed in them, and he washes him the third washing like the first and second. He wipes his abdomen in the first washing with a gentle wiping so that whatever residue may have remained in his belly may come out, such that had he not expelled it by wiping it would come out after the ghusl and thereby be invalidated, or come out in his shrouds. Likewise, he wipes his abdomen in the second washing. If anything comes out from him in the two washings, he removes it from its outlet and whatever of it has touched his body with water. He does not wipe his abdomen in the third washing.

key_terms.السِّدْرِ: lotus leaves used in the first washing water
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction toward which the deceased is oriented
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor used in the second washing water
key_terms.الْكَفَنُ: the shroud used for the deceased
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person being prepared for burial
key_terms.عِمَامَةَ: the turban cloth used as part of the shrouding
key_terms.مَاءً قَرَاحًا: plain unmixed water used in washing

ai.seo_question: How is the deceased washed and shrouded according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This narration discusses rulings and procedure related to the shrouding and ghusl of the deceased. It details the materials of the kafan, the orientation of the deceased toward the qiblah, the sequence of cleansing, wudu (ablution), and the three washings with sidr, camphor, and plain water. It is significant as a jurisprudential text outlining funeral purification in detail.
